Author-supplied atomic action for post-session verification.

longer ``description`` for nuance. ``id`` is the step's PERMANENT
identity: a client that has one (from a prior read, or client-minted at
authoring) sends it back and the server keeps it verbatim; the server
mints one (slugified from name) only when it is absent. It is therefore
optional on request inputs but always populated on response payloads —
the JSONB column on ``Assignment.steps`` carries the id back through
``from_attributes``. Use ``AssignmentStepResolved`` where an id MUST be

CreateEnvironmentVersionRequest.description:
Author a new variant of an environment.

``version`` is absent by design: it is server-assigned as max+1. No surveyed
platform lets the user author the immutable version identifier (ADR-0027's
survey), and users get NAMED things over auto counters — which is what
``label`` is.

``is_default`` is absent too: the default pointer moves only through the
dedicated ``set-default`` endpoint, so clear-then-set lives in exactly one
place. Authoring a variant therefore never silently redirects traffic.

validator level, the same shape ``InteractiveIterationDetails`` uses for its
platform↔field coupling. ``extra="forbid"``: a silently-ignored config key is
a customer debugging a target that was never set.

EnvironmentDescriptor.description:
An ad-hoc environment, described inline on the session that uses it.

Also the shape of the FROZEN SNAPSHOT a session carries after it was opened
against a REGISTERED environment (``environment_id``), which is why the field
is still named ``platform``: it holds the environment's ``kind``, and renaming a
live public field to match the newer internal vocabulary would break clients
for no behavioural gain.

platform.description: The kind of surface (e.g. `web`, `device`, `world`). Open union: new values may be added over time; clients must tolerate unknown values rather than failing on them.

EnvironmentDescriptor.title: EnvironmentDescriptor

EnvironmentKind.description:
What KIND of surface a registered environment is (ADR-0026).

Deliberately NOT called "platform": four incompatible platform vocabularies
already exist (``InteractiveIterationDetails.platform`` =
browser/android/ios/figma/code, ``FrameSourceType``, ``DEVICE_PLATFORMS``,
and the session lane's own free string) and they share no member. ``kind`` is
the one closed vocabulary the environment object owns; the lane-local ones
are mapped at their boundaries, never merged.

The member set is the session lane's MEASURED usage (dev ``sessions``
holds exactly ``web``, ``device``, ``world``; the old ``EnvironmentDescriptor``
docstring's "game" is ``world``). It is GROWABLE and stored as a VARCHAR, not
a Postgres enum: adding a kind must not need an ``ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE``
(which also forces a new staging boundary in
``scripts/test_db/upgrade_stages.sh``). Same posture as ``ApiKeyScope``.

Closed on the WRITE path (the request DTO parses through this enum), OPEN on
the READ path (responses type ``kind`` as ``str``): a row written by a newer
server carrying an unknown kind must still read back rather than fail
validation. That asymmetry IS the open-union contract the public DTOs
document via ``_OPEN_UNION_NOTE``.

UpdateAssignmentRequest.description:
Partial update: an omitted field is left alone.

``None`` is a real value for the NULLABLE fields — ``background`` and
``steps`` — where it CLEARS the column, so "omitted" and "explicitly null"
must stay distinguishable: the router reads ``model_fields_set``. ``name``
and ``goal`` are non-nullable; an explicit null there asserts nothing and
leaves the stored value alone.

Any applied write bumps ``revision`` (the audit counter); the content sha
frozen on each session is what keeps metadata-only bumps from splitting
usage series.

UpdateEnvironmentRequest.description:
Partial update: an omitted field is left alone.

``None`` is a real value for the NULLABLE fields — ``slug`` and
``operating_notes`` — where it CLEARS the column, so "omitted" and
"explicitly null" must stay distinguishable: the router reads
``model_fields_set`` rather than testing for None. ``kind`` is updatable but
re-validates the config against the NEW kind, so a web→device switch that
leaves only a ``url`` behind is a 422 rather than a broken row.

``example_actions`` is NOT NULL since Phase A, so null is not a way to clear
it and is REJECTED rather than silently ignored — send ``[]``. ``name``,
``kind`` and ``config`` are likewise non-nullable; an explicit null there
asserts nothing and leaves the stored value alone.

bearerAuth.description: Workspace API key as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer ish_sk_live_...`. Keys are workspace-scoped machine principals minted in Settings > Developers (shown once at mint). Scopes: `sessions:run` (create a session, submit turns, close), `sessions:read` (read the session and trace), `environments:read` and `environments:write` (manage the workspace's registered environments). A key is minted with the two `sessions:*` scopes by default; the `environments:*` pair must be requested. An ish user access token also works on the same header for personal scripts.

info.description:
The ish Developer API: the entry point for getting human feedback on whatever you're building, in whichever format you need.

Its first surface is **sessions**: you open a session for one of your personas inside *your own* environment, submit what the persona perceives (human-sensory observations: a rendered screen, an error message) along with the set of actions your environment currently offers, and the persona decides one action per turn and tells you how it felt. Your code executes the chosen action and loops. The environment loop is decide-only; ish never locates or executes anything in your environment (see ADR-0020/0021).

## Vocabulary

The public vocabulary is **workspace**, **persona**, **environment**, and **session**, and the wire uses these names directly:

- `workspace_id`: the workspace that owns the persona and is billed for the   session (the create path is `/workspaces/{workspace_id}/sessions`).
- `persona_id`: the persona the session drives.
- `environment_id`: a registered environment in that workspace — a named target   with its own operating notes and default action vocabulary. Register one and   reference it, or describe an ad-hoc one inline on the session; supply exactly   one of the two.

**"Session" here means one API session: a single persona working toward one goal in your environment, turn by turn.** It is not the ish product's notion of a study session (a person sitting down with a study), and it is unrelated to a browser session. Sessions live under `/v1/sessions`.

## Authentication

All requests use a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The token is a **workspace API key** (prefix `ish_sk_live_`), a workspace-scoped machine principal minted in Settings > Developers and shown exactly once at mint. Scopes: `sessions:run` (create, submit turns, close), `sessions:read` (read the session and trace), and `environments:read` / `environments:write` for the environment registry. Keys are minted with the two `sessions:*` scopes; ask for `environments:*` explicitly. An ish user access token (JWT) also works on the same header for personal scripts; server integrations should use keys.

## Versioning & forward-compatibility

The API is versioned in the URL path (`/api/v1`). Several enum-typed and block-typed fields are **open unions**: new values may be added over time, and clients MUST tolerate values they do not recognize rather than failing on them. The field descriptions call these out.

## Correlation & errors

Every response carries an **`X-Request-Id`** header; quote it in support requests. Error responses additionally echo it in the body as `request_id`.

Two error-body shapes exist; parse defensively, they differ:

- **`ValidationError`**: the request-validation layer (HTTP 422): a malformed   body (wrong types, missing fields, an invalid observation `type`, a bad enum   value, `parameters` that don't fit the model). A field-level envelope   (`error_code`, `errors[]`, `suggestions[]`; `suggestions` is CLI-oriented   boilerplate; ignore it for API use).
- **`Error`**: everything else, a `{ detail, request_id }` envelope. This   covers the handler layer's business-rule 422s (e.g. `exactly one image   observation block is required`; `persona has no renderable background`) as well   as 401 / 403 / 404 / 409 / 502. `detail` may be a structured object carrying a   machine-readable `error_kind` (e.g. `idempotency_conflict`,   `turn_index_mismatch`, `decision_invalid`).

That is why 422 is documented on the responses below as either shape (`oneOf`).
info.title: ish Developer API

delete.description:
Delete an assignment — an ARCHIVE under the hood (ADR-0028).

``archived_at`` is stamped, the row stays readable by id, sessions bound to
it keep resolving, and the name is freed for reuse. Idempotent. Refused
(409) while a PUBLISHED listing references the assignment: the listing's
task set is a live, paid contract and archiving would silently shrink it.

422.description: Validation error. A request-shape failure uses the `ValidationError` envelope; a handler-raised domain-validation refusal uses the `Error` envelope.

get.description: Fetch one assignment by id (archived rows stay readable).

422.description: Validation error. A request-shape failure uses the `ValidationError` envelope; a handler-raised domain-validation refusal uses the `Error` envelope.

patch.description:
Partially update an assignment; any applied write bumps ``revision``.

Sessions already opened against the old content are untouched — their goal
and revision are frozen on the session row (ADR-0028).

422.description: Validation error. A request-shape failure uses the `ValidationError` envelope; a handler-raised domain-validation refusal uses the `Error` envelope.

delete.description:
Archive a variant.

ARCHIVE, not hard delete, for the reason the parent archives: sessions
stamped with this version must keep resolving, and a comparison read over
historical runs must keep working. The row stays readable by id, appears in
the list under ``include_archived=true``, refuses new sessions, loses the
default pointer if it held it, and frees its label for reuse.

Idempotent: archiving an already-archived version is another 204.

422.description: Validation error. A request-shape failure uses the `ValidationError` envelope; a handler-raised domain-validation refusal uses the `Error` envelope.

get.description: One declared variant. Archived versions stay individually readable.

422.description: Validation error. A request-shape failure uses the `ValidationError` envelope; a handler-raised domain-validation refusal uses the `Error` envelope.

patch.description:
Partially update a variant. Omitted fields are untouched.

METADATA (``label``, ``description``) is editable for the life of the row.
``config`` and ``example_actions`` are FROZEN once any session has run
against this version: editing them then would retroactively relabel stored
runs, so the answer is a new version.

409.description: `detail.error_kind` is `environment_version_config_frozen` when `config`/`example_actions` are edited after a session has used this version, `environment_version_label_taken` on a label collision, or `environment_version_archived` when the version has been archived.

422.description: Validation error. A request-shape failure uses the `ValidationError` envelope; a handler-raised domain-validation refusal uses the `Error` envelope.

post.description:
Point this environment's default at this variant.

Sessions that name the environment WITHOUT pinning a version resolve here
from now on. Sessions already opened are untouched: the version they ran
against is stamped on the row and nothing re-resolves it.

Idempotent, and the outgoing default is cleared in the same transaction.

409.description: `detail.error_kind` is `environment_version_archived` — an archived version cannot become the default, since it refuses the very sessions the pointer would send it — or `environment_version_default_conflict` when a concurrent set-default won the race (retry after re-reading).

422.description: Validation error. A request-shape failure uses the `ValidationError` envelope; a handler-raised domain-validation refusal uses the `Error` envelope.

delete.description:
Delete an environment.

The wire contract is unchanged (204, and the environment stops appearing in
the list), but since ADR-0024 Phase A this ARCHIVES under the hood rather
than hard-deleting: ``archived_at`` is stamped, the row stays readable by id,
and a session's ``environment_id`` keeps resolving instead of being SET NULL.
A decision trace therefore never points at a dangling reference, and usage
aggregated on ``(environment_id, revision)`` survives the delete.

This supersedes ADR-0026's pre-launch hard delete via that ADR's own
deference clause to the concept spec. The name and address are freed for

post.description:
Open a decide-only session for a workspace/platform persona.

Supports the standard ``Idempotency-Key`` header: a retry with the same key
and body replays the existing session (200 instead of 201); the same key
with a different body is a 409 ``idempotency_conflict``.

The ASSIGNMENT (the session's intent, ADR-0028) is a required union of
exactly one shape: ``{"goal": ...}`` describes it inline, ``{"id": ...}``
binds a registered assignment — its goal and revision are FROZEN onto the
session at create, so later registry edits never touch it. An unreachable
or nonexistent assignment id is a 404; an ARCHIVED one is a 409
``assignment_archived``.

The environment comes in one of two forms (exactly one, enforced by the
request validator): a registered ``environment_id``, or an inline
``environment`` descriptor. A registered id is resolved within this workspace
and its name, kind and revision are SNAPSHOT onto the session (ADR-0024) — an
unreachable or nonexistent id is a 404, an ARCHIVED one is a 409
``environment_archived``, since the id resolves but the environment is retired.

200.description: Idempotent replay: an existing session was returned because the Idempotency-Key and request body matched a prior create.

403.description: The persona is out of scope for an external-environment session (ADR-0022: workspace-owned or platform-library personas only).

404.description: The workspace (`workspace_id`), persona (`persona_id`), environment (`environment_id`), or assignment (`assignment.id`) was not found or is not reachable by this principal.

409.description: The create was refused; `detail.error_kind` says why: `idempotency_conflict` (the Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request body), `environment_archived` (the environment resolves but is retired), or `assignment_archived` (the assignment resolves but is retired — register a new assignment, or pass the goal inline).

422.description: Validation error. A request-shape failure uses the `ValidationError` envelope; a handler-raised domain-validation refusal uses the `Error` envelope.

429.description: Per-key session-create quota exceeded (API keys only); transient, retry later.
